message.content:
Java is a **high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented** programming language created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now Oracle) and first shipped in 1995. Its core design goal has always been “write once, run anywhere” – code written in Java compiles into bytecode that executes on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), allowing programs to run unchanged across many operating systems and hardware platforms.

Key characteristics:

| Feature | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Platform independent** | Same compiled `.class` files work on Windows, macOS, Linux, embedded devices, etc., via the JVM. |
| **Strongly typed & safe** | Compile‑time type checking prevents many runtime errors; automatic bounds checks guard against buffer overflows. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Garbage collector frees unused objects automatically, reducing manual `malloc/free` bugs. |
| **Rich standard library** | Includes collections, networking, I/O streams, cryptography, XML/JSON parsing, GUI frameworks (`Swing`, `JavaFX`). |
| **Multithreading built‑in** | Thread API plus higher‑level constructs (`ExecutorService`, `CompletableFuture`) simplify concurrent programming. |
| **Security sandbox** | Applets and app‑let security policies restrict file/network access unless explicitly granted. |

Typical use cases include:

* Enterprise back‑end servers (Spring Boot, Jakarta EE)
* Desktop GUIs (`Swing`, `JavaFX`)
* Mobile apps for Android (via Kotlin/Java interop)
* Big data processing (Apache Hadoop, Spark)
* Embedded systems and IoT devices
* Scientific computing libraries

In addition to being a popular general‑purpose language, Java’s ecosystem includes powerful build tools (Maven, Gradle), dependency managers, testing frameworks (JUnit, TestNG), and continuous integration pipelines—all contributing to its widespread adoption in industry today.
